literal: In the Yong'an era he served as Supervisor of the Feathered Forest.
idiomatic: During the Yong'an era he served as supervisor of the Feathered Forest guard.

literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, for merit in defending Henei he was granted the title Marquis of Yong'an.
idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, his defense of Henei earned him the title Marquis of Yong'an.

literal: Later he became Administrator of Puyang commandery.
idiomatic: He later became administrator of Puyang commandery.

literal: Prince of Pengcheng Shao of Wei brought him in as military adviser of the Grand Prefect's office; when Shao went out to garrison Dingzhou, he petitioned to have him made Administrator of Dingzhou.
idiomatic: Prince of Pengcheng Shao of Wei took him on as a Grand Prefect's military adviser; when Shao went to garrison Dingzhou, he had Yu made administrator of that province.

literal: When Jing'an denounced Jing Hao's irreverent words, he cited Yu's words as corresponding in agreement.
idiomatic: When Gao Jing'an denounced Jing Hao's irreverent talk, he cited Yu's words as corroboration.

literal: Yu divined and said: "At that time I covered Jing Hao's mouth with my sleeve, saying 'Brother, do not speak rashly.'"
idiomatic: Yu cast lots and said, "At the time I covered Jing Hao's mouth with my sleeve and said, 'Brother, do not speak rashly.'"

literal: When Jing Hao was questioned, his account matched exactly what Yu's divination had listed; he was spared.
idiomatic: When Jing Hao was questioned, his account matched Yu's divination exactly, and Yu was spared.

literal: Several others who had heard the same words were all exiled to distant places.
idiomatic: Several others who had heard the same remark were all exiled to distant regions.

literal: Yu died while serving as Governor of Xuzhou.
idiomatic: Yu died as governor of Xuzhou.

literal: Dugu Yongye, courtesy name Shiji, original surname Liu, a man of Zhongshan.
idiomatic: Dugu Yongye, courtesy name Shiji, was originally surnamed Liu and came from Zhongshan.

literal: His mother remarried into the Dugu clan; Yongye was orphaned young and, following his mother, was raised in the Dugu household, and therefore took their surname.
idiomatic: His mother remarried into the Dugu clan. Orphaned young, Yongye was raised in their household and took their surname.

literal: He remained among ordinary soldiers, talented and skilled at bow and horse.
idiomatic: He rose from the ranks of ordinary soldiers—capable, skilled with bow and horse.

literal: Selected and appointed Defender-in-Chief of Dingzhou's Six Provinces, he garrisoned Jinyang.
idiomatic: Chosen for promotion, he was made defender-in-chief of Dingzhou's six provinces and garrisoned Jinyang.

literal: Some praised his discernment and usefulness; Emperor Shizong spoke with him and was pleased, promoting him beyond normal rank to outer military aide in the Secretariat-Directorate.
idiomatic: Some praised his judgment. Emperor Shizong spoke with him, was pleased, and promoted him past the usual steps to outer military aide in the Secretariat-Directorate.

literal: At the start of Tianbao he was made Secretariat Vice-Director and Administrator of Yuzhou.
idiomatic: At the start of Tianbao he was made secretariat vice-director and administrator of Yuzhou.

literal: Yongye understood writing and reckoning and excelled at song and dance; he was greatly known to Emperor Xianzu.
idiomatic: Yongye was literate and numerate, excelled at song and dance, and came to Emperor Xianzu's notice.

literal: Early in Ganming he went out as right assistant commissioner of the Heyang Circuit, was transferred to Governor of Luozhou, then to left assistant with his governorship unchanged, and was given Regular Attendant of the Mounted Guard.
idiomatic: Early in Ganming he went out as right assistant commissioner on the Heyang circuit, became governor of Luozhou, then left assistant while keeping the governorship, and was given regular attendant of the mounted guard.

literal: Yiyang lay deep in enemy territory; Zhou men built a fortified stronghold at Heijian to cut the grain route, and Yongye also built a garrison to resist.
idiomatic: Yiyang lay deep in enemy country. The Zhou built a fortified post at Heijian to sever the grain route; Yongye built a matching garrison to hold them off.

literal: He governed the frontier with great prestige and authority and was promoted to circuit senior minister.
idiomatic: He governed the frontier with great prestige and was promoted to circuit senior minister.

literal: In Heqing year 3 Zhou troops raided Luozhou; Yongye feared Governor Duan Siwen could not hold on his own and galloped into Jinyong to help defend.
idiomatic: In Heqing year 3 the Zhou raided Luozhou. Yongye feared Governor Duan Siwen could not hold alone and galloped into Jinyong to reinforce the defense.

literal: The Zhou built earthen mounds and tunnels and fought dawn and dusk; after three weeks the great army arrived and the invaders withdrew.
idiomatic: The Zhou raised earthworks and dug tunnels and attacked day and night. After three weeks the main army arrived and the raiders withdrew.

literal: Yongye had long been in Henan and was skilled at winning over and pacifying; those who came over to him numbered in the tens of thousands.
idiomatic: Yongye had long served in Henan and was skilled at winning people over; defectors numbered in the tens of thousands.

literal: He chose two hundred as his claws and teeth; each time he led the van with few against many, and Zhou troops feared him.
idiomatic: He picked two hundred as his shock troops and always led the van with few against many; the Zhou learned to fear him.

literal: He was given Grand Master of Splendid Parallels of Third Rank and very generous rewards.
idiomatic: He was made grand master of splendid parallels of the third rank and richly rewarded.

literal: By nature upright and blunt, he did not associate with the powerful.
idiomatic: Blunt and upright by nature, he kept no company with the powerful.

literal: Hulü Guang sought two maidservants and failed to obtain them; he slandered Yongye at court.
idiomatic: Hulü Guang asked for two maidservants and was refused; he slandered Yongye at court.

literal: Late in Heqing he was summoned as Grand Minister of Studs and replaced by Qifu Guihe; the four borders then grew weak and the mood in Heyang and Luoyang turned restless.
idiomatic: Late in Heqing he was recalled as grand minister of studs and replaced by Qifu Guihe. The frontiers weakened at once, and Heyang and Luoyang grew restless.

literal: In Wuping year 3 he was sent to take Hulü Fengluo and was made right vice minister of the Northern Circuit and Governor of Youzhou.
idiomatic: In Wuping year 3 he was sent to take Hulü Fengluo and was made right vice minister of the northern circuit and governor of Youzhou.

literal: Soon afterward he was summoned as General-in-Chief of the Guards.
idiomatic: Soon after he was summoned as general-in-chief of the guards.

literal: The people of Heyang and Luoyang mostly missed Yongye; the court also found the border unsettled and restored Yongye as right vice minister of the Heyang Circuit and Governor of Luozhou.
idiomatic: The people of Heyang and Luoyang missed him. With the border again unsettled, the court restored Yongye as right vice minister of the Heyang circuit and governor of Luozhou.

literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou personally attacked Jinyong, and Yongye led troops to meet him.
idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou attacked Jinyong in person; Yongye marched out to meet him.

literal: He asked: "What eminent official is this, and what is he doing?"
idiomatic: He called out, "What great man is that, and what is he up to?"

literal: The Zhou men said: "His Majesty has come himself—why does our host not come out to receive the guest?"
idiomatic: The Zhou answered, "His Majesty has come in person. Why does our host not come out to greet his guest?"

literal: Yongye said: "The guest travels too swiftly—that is why I do not come out."
idiomatic: Yongye said, "The guest is moving too fast—that is why I stay inside."

literal: He then spent the whole night preparing two thousand horse troughs.
idiomatic: That night he had two thousand horse troughs prepared.

literal: When the Zhou heard of it they thought a great army was coming and lifted the siege and left.
idiomatic: The Zhou heard of it, assumed a great army was near, and lifted the siege.

literal: Yongye was promoted to Grand Prefect and enfeoffed as Prince of Linchuan.
idiomatic: Yongye was promoted to grand prefect and enfeoffed as Prince of Linchuan.

literal: He had thirty thousand armored troops; when he first heard of the defeat at Jinyang he requested to march north to attack, but his memorials slept unanswered and Yongye grew indignant.
idiomatic: He had thirty thousand armored men. At the first news of Jinyang's fall he asked to march north; his memorials went unanswered, and Yongye burned with indignation.

literal: When he also heard that Bingzhou had fallen and was pressed by the Zhou general Duke of Changshan, he sent his son Xuda to offer surrender to Zhou.
idiomatic: When Bingzhou fell too and the Zhou general Duke of Changshan pressed him, he sent his son Xuda to surrender to Zhou.

literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou granted Yongye the rank Pillar of State.
idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou made Yongye pillar of state.

literal: Late in Xuanzheng he went out as chief administrator of Xiangzhou.
idiomatic: Late in Xuanzheng he was sent out as chief administrator of Xiangzhou.

literal: In Elephant year 2 he was killed by campaigning general-in-chief Cui Yanmin.
idiomatic: In Elephant year 2 he was killed by campaigning general-in-chief Cui Yanmin.

literal: Fu Fu was a man of Tai'an.
idiomatic: Fu Fu came from Tai'an.

literal: His father Yuanying was Grand Master of Splendid Parallels and Governor of Northern Yu Province.
idiomatic: His father Yuanying was grand master of splendid parallels and governor of northern Yu province.

literal: Fu joined the army young and, through battle merit, gradually rose to Grand Prefect and chief of the Yongqiao tribal settlement.
idiomatic: Fu took the army young and rose by battle merit to grand prefect and chief of the Yongqiao tribal settlement.

literal: When the Zhou emperor advanced on Heyin, Fu crossed the bridge by night and entered to hold Zhongtan fortress.
idiomatic: When the Zhou emperor advanced on Heyin, Fu crossed the bridge at night and entered Zhongtan fortress to hold it.

literal: The south city fell, but he was besieged for twenty days and did not yield.
idiomatic: The south city fell, yet he held under siege for twenty days without yielding.

literal: When relief arrived the Zhou army withdrew; Fu said to circuit commissioner Qifu Guihe: "The enemy is worn out—I ask for two thousand elite cavalry to pursue them; victory is certain."
idiomatic: Relief came and the Zhou withdrew. Fu told circuit commissioner Qifu Guihe, "The enemy is spent. Give me two thousand elite cavalry to pursue, and the victory is ours."

literal: Guihe would not permit it.
idiomatic: Guihe refused.

literal: In Wuping year 6 he was made Governor of Eastern Yong Province.
idiomatic: In Wuping year 6 he was made governor of eastern Yong province.

literal: When Zhou troops pressed close he went out to fight and drove them back.
idiomatic: When Zhou troops pressed in he fought them off.

literal: The Zhou took Jinyang and captured circuit commissioner Wei Xianggui, using him to summon Fu, but Fu would not obey.
idiomatic: The Zhou took Jinyang and captured circuit commissioner Wei Xianggui, whom they sent to summon Fu; Fu refused.

literal: The Later Sovereign personally went to relieve Jinyang and made Fu right vice minister of the circuit.
idiomatic: The Later Sovereign marched in person to relieve Jinyang and made Fu right vice minister of the circuit.

literal: When Zhou troops came to raid he struck and drove them off.
idiomatic: When Zhou raiders came he struck and drove them off.

literal: The Zhou took Bingzhou and sent Wei Xiaokuan with his son Shikuan to summon Fu, saying: "Bingzhou is already pacified, so we send your son to report—submit at once."
idiomatic: The Zhou took Bingzhou and sent Wei Xiaokuan with his son Shikuan to summon Fu: "Bingzhou is pacified. We send your son with the news—submit now."

literal: They offered him Grand General and Duke of Wuxiang with an open state, gave him the patent on the spot, and sent two gold-and-agate wine vessels as tokens.
idiomatic: They offered him grand general and Duke of Wuxiang with an open state, handed him the patent at once, and sent two gold-and-agate wine vessels as tokens of faith.

literal: Fu would not accept and said to Xiaokuan: "To serve one's lord one has death but no second loyalty. This boy cannot exhaust loyalty as a subject or filial piety as a son—men loathe him. I ask that you cut off his head at once to proclaim it to the realm."
idiomatic: Fu refused and told Xiaokuan, "A subject owes his lord death, not divided loyalty. This boy is no loyal subject and no filial son—men despise him. Cut off his head now and proclaim it to the realm."

literal: The Zhou emperor returned from Ye to Jinyang and sent Gao Anaigong and more than a hundred others to the Fen River to summon Fu.
idiomatic: The Zhou emperor returned from Ye to Jinyang and sent Gao Anaigong and more than a hundred men to the Fen to summon Fu.

literal: Fu led his army out and, across the water, asked where His Majesty was now.
idiomatic: Fu marched out, met them across the water, and asked where His Majesty was.

literal: Anaigong said: "He has already been captured and is entering the passes by another route."
idiomatic: Anaigong said, "He is already captured and entering the passes by another road."

literal: Fu looked up to heaven and wept loudly, led his troops into the city, and before the audience hall faced north and wailed for a long time before he submitted.
idiomatic: Fu looked up and wept aloud, led his men into the city, and before the audience hall faced north and wailed a long while before he submitted.

literal: When the Zhou emperor saw him he said: "Why did you not submit sooner?"
idiomatic: The Zhou emperor saw him and said, "Why did you not submit sooner?"

literal: Fu wept as he answered: "For three generations my house has eaten Qi grain and been entrusted as I was; I could not die in the revolution—I am ashamed to face heaven and earth."
idiomatic: Fu answered through tears, "Three generations of my house ate Qi grain and were trusted as I was. I could not die in the revolution—I am ashamed to face heaven and earth."

literal: The Zhou emperor personally took his hand and said: "A subject should be like this."
idiomatic: The Zhou emperor took his hand and said, "This is how a subject should be."

literal: "In pacifying Qi I have seen only you."
idiomatic: "In pacifying Qi I have seen only you."

literal: He himself ate a lamb rib and gave Fu the bone, saying: "Bone is kin to kin; flesh is distant—that is why I give this to you."
idiomatic: He ate a lamb rib himself and gave Fu the bone, saying, "Bone is kin to kin; flesh is distant—that is why I entrust this to you."

literal: He then led Fu aside to eat with him, had him lodge with the attendant guard, granted him Grand Master of Splendid Parallels, and charged him: "If I at once give you high office I fear those who come over will waver—work hard and have no fear of wealth and honor."
idiomatic: He drew Fu aside to eat with him, lodged him with the attendant guard, made him grand master of splendid parallels, and charged him, "If I give you high rank at once, those who surrender will waver. Serve well—you will not lack wealth or honor."

literal: He also asked what office he had received for saving Heyin before.
idiomatic: He also asked what office Fu had received for holding Heyin before.

literal: Fu said: "I received one promotion—Special Advancement and Duke of Yongchang with an open state."
idiomatic: Fu said, "One promotion—special advancement and Duke of Yongchang with an open state."

literal: The Zhou emperor said to the Later Sovereign: "Three years ago I trained troops and resolved to take Heyin, but because Fu Fu could hold it the city would not move, so I withdrew the army."
idiomatic: The Zhou emperor told the Later Sovereign, "Three years ago I drilled troops and meant to take Heyin, but Fu Fu held the city and it would not budge, so I withdrew."

literal: "Your rewards then were how meager!"
idiomatic: "Your reward then was how meager!"

literal: He gave Fu a gold wine cup.
idiomatic: He gave Fu a gold wine cup.

literal: Later he was made Governor of Minzhou and soon died.
idiomatic: He was later made governor of Minzhou and soon died.

literal: After the Qi army's defeat at Jinyang, few commanders and generals kept their integrity whole.
idiomatic: After the Qi defeat at Jinyang, few officers kept their honor intact.

literal: Among those who died to perfect loyalty was Grand Master of Splendid Parallels Chigan Gousheng, who garrisoned southern Yan Province; when the Zhou emperor took Ye and the amnesty arrived, Gousheng hanged himself.
idiomatic: Among those who died to perfect loyalty was grand master of splendid parallels Chigan Gousheng, garrisoning southern Yan province. When the Zhou took Ye and the amnesty arrived, Gousheng hanged himself.

literal: There was also Grand Prefect and Palace Attendant eunuch Tian Jingxuan, original name Peng, a barbarian.
idiomatic: There was also grand prefect and palace attendant eunuch Tian Jingxuan, originally named Peng, a barbarian.

literal: At fourteen or fifteen he loved reading.
idiomatic: At fourteen or fifteen he loved books.

literal: Once in the palace service he seized every chance to inquire urgently; each time he reached the Hall of Forested Literature he would gasp and sweat, and beyond asking about books he had no leisure for other talk.
idiomatic: Once in palace service he seized every chance to study. Each visit to the Hall of Forested Literature left him gasping and drenched in sweat; beyond books he had no time for anything else.

literal: When he read of ancient men's integrity he never failed to be moved and linger over it.
idiomatic: When he read of ancient integrity he was always moved to long reflection.

literal: Yan Zhitui prized his diligence in study and greatly encouraged him; he later rose to prominence.
idiomatic: Yan Zhitui prized his diligence and encouraged him generously; he later rose to prominence.

literal: When the Later Sovereign fled to Qingzhou he sent Jingxuan west to observe movements and was captured by Zhou troops.
idiomatic: When the Later Sovereign fled to Qingzhou he sent Jingxuan west to watch the enemy and was taken by Zhou troops.

literal: Asked where the Qi sovereign was, he lied that he had already gone.
idiomatic: Asked where the Qi sovereign was, he lied that the emperor had already gone.

literal: They beat him until he confessed; with each limb broken his words and color grew fiercer, and in the end all four limbs were broken off and he died.
idiomatic: They beat him to make him confess; with each limb broken his voice and bearing grew fiercer, until all four were severed and he died.

literal: There was also Lei Xianhe, who after the defeat at Jinyang became left vice minister of the Jianzhou Circuit.
idiomatic: There was also Lei Xianhe, who after Jinyang's fall became left vice minister of the Jianzhou circuit.

literal: The Zhou emperor had his son summon him, but Xianhe restrained his son and would not accept.
idiomatic: The Zhou emperor sent his son to summon him; Xianhe restrained his son and refused.

literal: When he heard that Ye had fallen he submitted.
idiomatic: When he heard Ye had fallen he submitted.

literal: After the Later Sovereign lost Bingzhou he sent Grand Prefect Hexi Yong'an to urge emergency aid on the Türk qaghan Tabo.
idiomatic: After the Later Sovereign lost Bingzhou he sent grand prefect Hexi Yong'an to beg emergency aid of the Türk qaghan Tabo.

literal: When he heard that Qi had perished, Tabo placed Yong'an under a Tuyuhun envoy.
idiomatic: When he heard Qi had perished, Tabo placed Yong'an under a Tuyuhun envoy.

literal: Yong'an spoke boldly: "Our state is already defeated—would Yong'an spare a worthless life!"
idiomatic: Yong'an spoke boldly: "Our state is already defeated—would I spare a worthless life!"

literal: "I wished to hold my breath and end myself, but feared the realm would not know that Great Qi had a subject who died for principle—I ask only for one blade to show the distant and near."
idiomatic: "I meant to hold my breath and die, but feared the world would not know Great Qi had a subject who died on principle. Give me one blade to show far and near."

literal: Tabo admired his fierce loyalty, gave him seventy horses, and sent him home.
idiomatic: Tabo admired his courage, gave him seventy horses, and sent him home.

literal: Gao Baoning, a man of Dai, of unknown origin.
idiomatic: Gao Baoning came from Dai; his origins are unknown.

literal: Late in Wuping he was Governor of Ying Province, garrisoning Huanglong; barbarians and Chinese alike respected his prestige.
idiomatic: Late in Wuping he was governor of Ying province, garrisoning Huanglong; barbarians and Chinese alike respected his authority.

literal: As Zhou troops were about to reach Ye, Youzhou circuit commissioner Pan Zihuang led Huanglong troops down; Baoning led elite cavalry together with Khitan and Mohe—more than ten thousand horsemen—to march to the rescue.
idiomatic: As Zhou troops neared Ye, Youzhou circuit commissioner Pan Zihuang led Huanglong troops down. Baoning led elite cavalry with Khitan and Mohe—more than ten thousand horsemen—to the rescue.

literal: Reaching Beiping he learned Zihuang had already set out from Ji and also heard that the capital Ye was lost, and returned to camp.
idiomatic: At Beiping he learned Zihuang had already marched from Ji and that Ye had fallen; he turned back to camp.

literal: The Zhou emperor sent envoys to summon and reassure him; he would not accept the edict.
idiomatic: The Zhou emperor sent envoys to reassure him; he would not accept the edict.

literal: Prince of Fanyang Shaoyi was among the Türks and submitted a memorial urging accession; Fanyang appointed Baoning chancellor.
idiomatic: Prince of Fanyang Shaoyi was with the Türks and submitted a memorial urging accession; Fanyang appointed Baoning chancellor.

literal: When Lu Changqi held Fanyang city and rose in arms, Baoning brought Shaoyi to gather barbarian and Chinese troops—tens of thousands of horsemen—to rescue him.
idiomatic: When Lu Changqi seized Fanyang and rose in arms, Baoning brought Shaoyi to gather tens of thousands of barbarian and Chinese horsemen to relieve the city.

literal: Reaching the Lu River he learned the Zhou general Yuwen Shenju had already slaughtered Fanyang; he returned to hold Huanglong and in the end would not serve Zhou.
idiomatic: At the Lu River he learned Zhou general Yuwen Shenju had already sacked Fanyang. He withdrew to hold Huanglong and never submitted to Zhou.

literal: The historiographer says: Pi Jinghe and the others came from the hegemonic foundation, enrolled their names in the military camp, passed through hardship and peril to the final age, held high rank and heavy responsibility, and all fulfilled their original loyalty—each also met his time.
idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Pi Jinghe and the others rose from the hegemonic foundation, took their names into the war camp, passed through hardship to the dynasty's end, held high rank and heavy trust, and each kept faith to the end—they too met their hour.
